body_text:
Japan faces a difficult security environment. Relations with the rising superpower next door, namely China, are extremely tense at present and for the last year. Japan must also contend with a hostile Russia and North Korea as well. All three of these countries possess nuclear weapons and are actively adding to those arsenals. If that wasn’t enough, the second Trump administration has been distracted by the Middle East and also demonstrated a relatively carefree approach to traditional U.S. allies.

No wonder that nuclear talk is now fashionable among defense analysts in Tokyo.

Indeed, Japan has good reasons to take its defense more seriously and has set about doing so. For decades, Tokyo restricted itself to spending about 1% of GDP on defense, but that self-imposed restriction fell away in recent years. Today, serious calculations are underway regarding whether or not Japan should follow other middle powers like Australia and South Korea by creating a nuclear submarine program. While the idea is not without merit, Japanese and American strategists need to consider the wider consequences before stepping out on this new initiative.

In early November, the Chinese newspaper Global Times published an editorial revealing that China’s rather predictable reaction to any Japanese plan to build a nuclear submarine force would be extremely harsh. The editorial suggests that Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi has “become obsessed” with acquiring nuclear submarines. The Chinese article is sharply critical of the initiative, explaining that it represents a “sleight of hand intended to bypass scrutiny.” It explains: “The fuel cycle, the reprocessing of spent nuclear fuel, and the management of nuclear materials associated with nuclear-powered submarines overlap significantly with the development path for nuclear weapons.”

This Chinese perspective interprets Japan’s strategy as follows: Acquire the submarines first, then obtain nuclear weapons — presumably following a secret roadmap by “right-wing factions.”

The same editorial also had harsh words for the United States, asserting, “The United States is well aware of this, yet it has long chosen to turn a blind eye.” According to this rendering, Washington leaders “seek to arm Japan, transforming it into a forward-deployed spearhead in East Asia and forcing it to shoulder a greater share of the costs of confrontation.”

The piece concludes that U.S. policy is “shortsighted and arrogant … [as it] gambles with the post-war international order and the nuclear non-proliferation regime, effectively allowing a dangerous ‘Pandora’s box’ to be pried open.”

The shrill tone of this editorial is worthy of note. China-Japan relations have entered a genuine crisis stage during the last year and Washington must be cognizant of the perilous escalatory dynamics, since it could unfortunately be dragged into an unwanted war between the two contending East Asian powers.

To be sure, there are reasons why Japanese nuclear submarines merit closer analysis. Not only is the Chinese Navy’s rapid growth altering the Asia-Pacific military balance, but Japan could quite seamlessly integrate into the existing AUKUS program, a Biden administration initiative from 2021 that unites America together with Australia and the U.K. to focus on jointly fabricating nuclear submarines.

Unquestionably, Tokyo does possess the requisite trained workforce and industrial capabilities to make such a force feasible, even in the near future. Nuclear submarines remain as a formidable naval weapons system – for sure. Finally, if the development of nuclear submarines can preclude the creation of Japanese nuclear weapons, that could perhaps form a sensible political compromise in this age of increasing insecurity.

At present, however, the counterarguments remain more compelling. Such a step by Tokyo would undoubtedly kick up a political firestorm both in the international community and most likely within Japan itself too. The Chinese editorial may be correct that opening “Pandora’s Box” and this route to nuclear weapons proliferation could initiate the much feared “nuclear cascade,” since many other countries may wish to go the same direction.

It’s also important to recognize that Japan already wields a very potent undersea force with some of the most advanced air-independent propulsion (AIP) diesel submarines in the world. True, nuclear submarines are generally larger and could carry a spate of new offensive weapons systems, such as land-attack missiles. But that would change the character of the Japanese Maritime Self-defense Force into a more offensive striking element, as opposed to a defensive force. A nuclear submarine fleet and associated offensive munitions (e.g. land-attack missiles) would soak up scarce resources for Japan’s crucial defensively-oriented, conventional forces and, moreover, much of the East Asian littoral has shallow waters that are not so amenable to larger nuclear submarines anyhow.

Most consequential, however, would be the obviously deleterious impact that this development would entail for China-Japan relations, as the above editorial makes clear. The sad but important reality of contemporary China-Japan relations is that this enmity is less based on divergent interests or aggressive intentions. Instead, the present hostility arises from dangerous, emotive historical grievances.

America cannot allow such unrequited nationalist impulses on either side of the East China Sea to escalate into a gravely hazardous “spiral model” of conflict. Therefore, Washington must reign in Tokyo’s ambitions for nuclear submarines, even as it encourages Japan to further develop defensive capabilities, such as air defenses, mine countermeasures, and base hardening consistent with the military lessons from the recent wars in the Persian Gulf and Eastern Europe.

Lyle Goldstein is director of the China Initiative at Brown University’s Watson School and concurrently serves as director of the Asia Program at the think-tank Defense Priorities.

title: Ravens didn't discipline receiver over a domestic arrest but deactivate Marlon Humphrey over podcast comments
excerpt:
Baltimore Ravens star Kyle Hamilton tells OutKick that the team has gotten "unlucky" but still has the capability to win games.

The Baltimore Ravens sent cornerback Marlon Humphrey home, and he will ...
body_text:
Baltimore Ravens star Kyle Hamilton tells OutKick that the team has gotten "unlucky" but still has the capability to win games.

The Baltimore Ravens sent cornerback Marlon Humphrey home, and he will not practice and will be deactivated for Sunday's game at the Carolina Panthers, coach Jesse Minter announced Thursday.

The reason for all this is apparently because Humphrey hurt some people's feelings.

"After a lot of internal conversations between obviously with myself and leadership of the organization, we decided to deactivate Marlon for this game this upcoming week," Minter told reporters at his regularly scheduled media availability. "And so, truthfully, I know there's going to be a lot of questions. Most of it, again, I said this yesterday, like these conversations are very, very personal and private, and to me, need to remain that for the good of the team and the organization."

Minter said the deactivation will be one game — "for now."

WHAT IS BALTIMORE BEST AT MAKING? 'CRIMINALS,' SAYS MARLON HUMPHREY WHO THEN FEELS THE HEAT AND CHANGES TUNE

Marlon Humphrey (44) of the Baltimore Ravens looks on during an NFL football game against the Detroit Lions at M&T Bank Stadium on Sept. 22, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Michael Owens/Getty Images)

RAVENS PLAYERS RIDE WITH PRESIDENT TRUMP IN MOTORCADE, GET SHOUTOUT DURING SPEECH AT BALTIMORE SHIPYARD EVENT

And it is not known if this deactivation had anything to do with an internal disagreement of any kind between Humphrey and club leadership beyond his words on his podcast this week.

But if there was no such internal club episode, what we have is the Baltimore Ravens suspending a good player who has started 123 games since joining the team in 2017 because he took liberties on his podcast this week in responding to the question, "What is Baltimore best at making?"

"They're best at making criminals," Humphrey said half-jokingly.

And, yes, that set off a lot of people in Baltimore. Some of those people are apparently within and outside the Ravens organization.

But Wednesday, Humphrey apologized for his off-the-cuff remark.

Los Angeles Chargers tight end Charlie Kolar makes a catch against Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore, Md., on Nov. 16, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

JOSH JACOBS 'REMORSEFUL' IN FIRST COMMENTS SINCE DOMESTIC ABUSE ARREST LED TO COMMISSIONER'S EXEMPT LIST STAY

"I do know the effect that words have," Humphrey told reporters surrounding his locker stall. "I'd just like to apologize for those comments."

Not enough, apparently. Baltimore mayor Brandon Scott went on his Instagram account and made Humphrey's comment about race.

The Ravens, obviously feeling community pressure, decided Humphrey's apology fell short of their pound-of-flesh disciplinary requirements.

"I would say this, you know, he's very remorseful," Minter said. "I think he really understands, you know, that words mean a lot, especially to the people in the city. And, you know, when you say something like that, it's not a reflection of our team and our organization and how we want to operate."

NFL RESTARTS SOCIAL JUSTICE MESSAGING WHILE BATTLING DOMESTIC ABUSE, DRUNK DRIVING AND PROSTITUTION ARRESTS

The Baltimore Ravens, struggling to rally after losing five consecutive games and watching their playoff hopes fade with every passing week, are sitting one of the better players because he said something dumb.

And this is where we understand precisely how preposterous this disciplinary action is: Compare it to how the Ravens handled receiver Rashod Batemen's charges tied to a domestic violence incident in June.

Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman (7) celebrates his touchdown scored against the Los Angeles Chargers with wide receiver Diontae Johnson (18) during the first half at SoFi Stadium on Nov. 25, 2024. (Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images)

Bateman was arrested on charges of first-degree criminal damage to property (felony property damage), battery (family violence), and reckless conduct after he allegedly used an object to smash the windshield and driver's side window of a Mercedes-Benz belonging to the mother of his child.

The woman and the couple's three-month-old child were inside the vehicle at the time.

3 NFL STARS HIT COMMISSIONER'S EXEMPT LIST AFTER OFFSEASON FILLED WITH LEGAL TROUBLE

Police reported that the woman sustained multiple cuts and contusions from the shattered glass, and the infant, sitting in a baby seat, had glass found on his hair, face and car seat.

Baltimore Ravens coach Jesse Minter attends the NFL Scouting Combine at the Indiana Convention Center in Indianapolis, Ind., on Feb. 24, 2026. (Kirby Lee/Imagn Images)

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

When news of the arrest and subsequent charges surfaced in August, during the team's training camp, the Ravens stated they had been aware of the situation, were in direct communication with Bateman, notified the NFL office, and were cooperating with the league and authorities while treating it as a pending legal matter.

The NFL opened a review of the matter but, meanwhile, the Ravens did not suspend, deactivate, or place Bateman on any disciplinary leave. And they still have not.

Also, Baltimore's mayor did not release a statement about Batemen and domestic abuse.

So the guy arrested on domestic abuse allegations has remained untouched so far. But the guy who said something arguably inappropriate (maybe) and apologized the next day, gets suspended one game "for now."

The Baltimore Ravens have totally lost the plot.

FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.

title: Iran-backed Houthi 'terrorist attack' hits Riyadh's tallest skyscraper and HQ of Saudi Public Investment Fund
excerpt: Houthi rebels strike in Yemen as Middle East tensions escalate. Hudson Institute senior fellow Rebecca Heinrichs joins 'America's Newsroom' to analyze the Iran-backed proxy threat and the latest updat...
body_text:
Houthi rebels strike in Yemen as Middle East tensions escalate. Hudson Institute senior fellow Rebecca Heinrichs joins 'America's Newsroom' to analyze the Iran-backed proxy threat and the latest updates on the war in Ukraine.

A "terrorist attack" by the Iran-backed Houthis damaged multiple floors at the tallest skyscraper in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, which houses the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund on Thursday, authorities and reports said.

Entrances leading into the King Abdullah Financial District were closed and people were being evacuated from the area following the strike by a suspected Houthi missile, according to Reuters.

The news agency reported that the attack on the Public Investment Fund Tower, which is 80 stories tall, destroyed windows across up to eight floors of the building and bent portions of its metal facade.

"One of the towers of the Financial Center in Riyadh was targeted in a terrorist attack by the terrorist Houthi militia, causing material damage but no injuries — praise be to God," the General Directorate of Saudi Civil Defense wrote on X as it shared a photo of the damage.

HOUTHIS KILL 14 AT SAUDI AIRPORT AS EXPERT WARNS OF 'RAPID TARGETS' AMID MIDDLE EAST WAR

The Public Investment Fund Tower in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, is the tallest skyscraper in the city. The building was seen damaged on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, following what officials called a "terrorist attack" by the Iran-backed Houthis. (General Directorate of Saudi Civil Defense)

The incident unfolded after the Houthis attacked a building belonging to Saudi state-owned oil company Aramco, in the same area on Nov. 8, Reuters reported.

Saudi-led coalition spokesman Col. Turki Al-Malki said Thursday that Saudi air defenses "intercepted and destroyed 4 ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi terrorist militia toward the southern region."

He also said the coalition went on offense in Yemen, destroying a ballistic missile launch platform in Dhamar that was used by the Houthis "in an attempt to attack Riydah today."

HOUTHIS EMERGE AS GLOBAL THREAT BEYOND IRAN CONTROL AMID SAUDI STRIKES, FORMER ENVOY WARNS

The KAFD World Trade Center, Riyadh Bank skyscraper office building, Public Investment Fund tower and Saudi National Bank headquarters stand beyond the King Abdullah Financial District Conference Center in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Tuesday, Dec. 6, 2022. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)

The Houthis have been escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia during the U.S.-Iran war.

The U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Saudi Arabia warned Americans earlier this week that they "should exercise heightened vigilance due to the increased threat of armed attacks by Iranian-supported Houthis and Iranian efforts to target U.S. government officials and facilities in the region.

"Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," it added. "These hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area."

Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Hillary Clinton accuses Trump of 'aiding and abetting' humanitarian crisis in Ukraine
excerpt:
Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton penned a New York Times piece criticizing President Donald Trump.  (Dominik Bindl/Getty Images; Mandel Ngan/AFP via Getty Images)

Former Secretary of State H...
body_text:
Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton penned a New York Times piece criticizing President Donald Trump.  (Dominik Bindl/Getty Images; Mandel Ngan/AFP via Getty Images)

Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton on Thursday said President Donald Trump appears to be "aiding and abetting" a humanitarian crisis in Ukraine, in a scathing New York Times op-ed.

The 2016 Democratic nominee for president penned a New York Times opinion piece headlined, "What Trump Should Have Said to Putin," that criticized Trump’s Thursday trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. The White House issued a "U.S.-Russia-China Heads of State Declaration toward Peace," which states that the three leaders intend to communicate on decreasing nuclear risks and preventing nuclear weapons proliferation – but Clinton isn’t satisfied.

"A strong, strategic American president should have demanded that the Russian military stop bombarding Ukrainian civilians and destroying their energy and water infrastructure," Clinton wrote.

TRUMP'S HISTORIC SUMMIT WITH XI, PUTIN MARKS DIPLOMATIC MILESTONE, BUT BREAKTHROUGHS REMAIN ELUSIVE

Chinese President Xi Jinping, President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin greet each other at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov. 18, 2026, in Shenzhen, China. (Iori Sagisawa-China Pool/Getty Images)

"He should have warned Mr. Xi that China will pay a price for providing support for Russia’s war machine," Clinton continued. "And he should have made it clear to Mr. Putin that his efforts to freeze the Ukrainian people into submission this winter will fail — because the Ukrainians are tougher than Mr. Putin thinks and because the United States and our NATO allies will redouble support to them."

Clinton then declared, "No one expected Mr. Trump to do any of this. Initial reports suggest that he didn’t."

Clinton accused Trump of making "excuses for Russia" when he said Putin could be even tougher on Ukraine.

"Over recent months, the United States has actually reduced its support for Ukraine," Clinton wrote, pointing to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's claims about disrupted Starshield access.

UKRAINE'S STARLINK RESTORED AS ELON MUSK CLAIMS KYIV VIOLATED TERMS OF SERVICE 'TO KILL PEOPLE'

President Donald Trump famously defeated Democratic nominee Hillary Clinton in the 2016 presidential election.  (Robyn Beck/AFP via Getty Images)

"The administration’s actions have emboldened the Russian dictator, making it less likely that he will make concessions for peace, and have undermined Ukraine’s ability to defend itself," Clinton wrote.

"In January, new Democratic majorities in Congress should investigate Mr. Trump’s appeasement of Russia and pressure him to provide more support to Ukraine," she continued. "But the people of Ukraine can’t wait that long."

Clinton wrote, "Ukrainian cities will be left without heat or power" this winter and Putin’s "apparent goal is to put millions of people at risk of freezing to death and to create a surge of refugees into the rest of Europe," before calling on "the current lame-duck Congress" to push Trump to help.

Clinton ended her opinion piece by declaring, "In January, the new Congress should go further and pass additional support for Ukraine to help it win this war. This is a time for action, not appeasement."

TRUMP IS TRYING ‘THE ART OF THE DEAL’ IN UKRAINE BUT WHAT MUST PUTIN GIVE UP?

Vladimir Putin and President Donald Trump shake hands as leaders take a group photo during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit in Shenzhen. (Sergei Bobylyov/Pool/AFP via Getty Images)

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Heritage Action media fellow Tim Young mocked "one of the architects of the Russian hoax" for weighing in on what the president should have said to Putin.

"Every time I see Hillary Clinton say something like what the president ‘should do,’ I’m reminded of her social media post saying, ‘happy birthday’ to a future president with a picture of a younger her," Young told Fox News Digital. "It just shows she’s jealous she’s not there."

Young also suggested that Clinton’s comments prove "it’s not only Republicans who learned nothing from the midterms."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"What is clear from her comments is that she is pro-forever war with Ukraine and Russia, and wars are the opposite of what the American people want," Young said.

Fox News Digital’s Alex Nitzberg contributed to this report.

Brian Flood is a media editor/reporter for FOX News Digital. Story tips can be sent to brian.flood@fox.com and on Twitter: @briansflood.

title: Call for police to investigate Scottish hospital after 19 deaths due to surgery
excerpt:
Surgeon at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary says he repeatedly voiced concerns that patients may have died unnecessarily

A senior surgeon has called for a criminal investigation into a Scottish hospital afte...
body_text:
Surgeon at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary says he repeatedly voiced concerns that patients may have died unnecessarily

A senior surgeon has called for a criminal investigation into a Scottish hospital after it emerged that at least 19 patients had died from avoidable complications due to surgery.

Dr Mohammed Habib, a consultant at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary, said he had repeatedly reported concerns about the hospital’s liver and pancreatic surgery from 2021 onwards and believed dozens of patients may have died unnecessarily there.

Calling for a police investigation into corporate homicide at the hospital, Habib alleged that senior officials at NHS Grampian, the crisis-hit health board which runs it, failed to take the correct action quickly enough.

Habib said NHS Grampian eventually commissioned an expert report to investigate his allegations, and those from a second whistleblower, which confirmed his allegations that 19 patients had died due to “serious adverse events” caused by surgery between 2015 and 2021.

Their internal report was published on Thursday by Habib’s solicitor, Aamer Anwar.

Habib’s comments and the findings were discussed in Holyrood later on Thursday. John Swinney, Scotland’s first minister, said Habib’s disclosures were “of the gravest concern”. The NHS had legal duties to give patients the best possible care and to quickly investigate allegations about safety failures, he said.

But he rebuffed demands from Michael Marra, the Scottish Labour leader, for a criminal investigation into the “systemic failures” at NHS Grampian.

Speaking at first minister’s questions, Marra said the families of the 19 people who died “deserve answers and deserve justice.”

Swinney denied that the government had ignored Habib’s complaints and said the recent decision to demand changes of leadership and urgent reforms at the board should produce the necessary improvements.

Laura Skaife-Knight, chief executive of NHS Grampian, said: “We are aware of the serious allegations raised today. A thorough investigation has already taken place into these matters, with some elements of that work ongoing. Any new evidence or information will be carefully considered, and NHS Grampian will continue to respond through the appropriate clinical, governance and legal processes.

“We understand the allegations will cause further concern to patients, members of the public and staff. It is important we respect patient and employee confidentiality, but we can highlight that where reviews identify issues around patient care, the appropriate duty of candour processes are followed. This includes direct communication with patients and families where required.

“If our consideration of any new evidence identifies further individuals who should be contacted, we will do so. Patient safety remains our highest priority.”

The two external experts who carried out the review in 2022, surgery professors at Edinburgh and Leeds universities, concluded the “extremely high” death rate at Aberdeen between 2017 and 2020 ran as high as 18% within liver and pancreatic surgery.

It said the national average for surgery-related fatalities was 2-3% for that speciality, depending on the patient’s condition.

The surgeon, who still works at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary, said the unit continued operating on patients. He then flagged the cases of four other patients who had died during or after surgery since that expert report was completed.

In March 2026, another external expert said it was imperative that surgery ended there, telling hospital executives its “persistent high mortality in complex surgery is a red-flag indicator of systemic failure”. The liver and pancreatic surgery department was then shut down.

Based on the fatality calculations made in 2022, Habib said dozens of patients may have died unnecessarily at the hospital.

He said he had repeatedly contacted the police, Scottish government ministers and Scotland’s independent whistleblowing officer, but was fobbed off, or told the cases he raised were time-barred.

His allegations are the latest in a series of medical and managerial crises at NHS Grampian, which has led to paediatric surgery at Gray’s hospital being shut down, the replacement of the board’s chairperson and its medical director, and independent investigations into other serious adverse events at its hospitals.

Last week, Angela Constance, the Scottish health secretary, told MSPs there were extremely serious systemic problems with mismanagement and underperformance at NHS Grampian.

In a statement at Holyrood, she told MSPs the health board faced being put into special measures if its current reforms were not introduced quickly or effectively enough.

Last week, a report by Healthcare Improvement Scotland (HIS), an NHS watchdog, found “very serious shortcomings with NHS Grampian’s leadership”, which included failing to be transparent and accurate in its accounts of its actions.

There had been “persistent, serious concerns about safety, quality, clinical governance and leadership” at the board, it said.

However, the HIS report only identified one patient death due to a serious adverse event.

Habib and Anwar said the evidence from the expert review into Habib’s unit had shown many more deaths were avoidable, and that this raised their concerns about whether the full extent of the crisis at NHS Grampian was being covered up.

Habib said NHS Grampian is “avoiding accountability by not being transparent about what damage has been done, while promising heaven and earth going forward.

“In every other death at the hands of the state, families would be entitled to understand the circumstances of their loved ones’ death. [They] deserve to know how and why their loved one died.”

Anwar said the Lord Advocate, Ruth Charteris KC, should instruct her lawyers and Police Scotland to launch a criminal investigation. Ministers should immediately place NHS Grampian into special measures, he added.

There was a “catastrophic failure to act” at NHS Grampian, Anwar said. “While the Grampian leadership was busy burying evidence behind complex medical jargon, they also failed to explain to bereaved families that their loved ones had died after the wrong operation.”

A Scottish government spokesperson said: “We recognise the courage shown by this whistleblower to raise concerns. Everyone who works in our NHS should feel safe and supported to speak up without fear of detriment.

“Ministers have already committed to transparently setting out all engagement with NHS Grampian in relation to the concerns raised in the HIS Review.

“The government took action and repeatedly raised the concerns of Dr Habib with both Healthcare Improvement Scotland and NHS Grampian. As the HIS review set out last week, there were clear failures in the former medical leadership and in how concerns were being addressed within NHS Grampian.

“NHS Grampian is now subject to a very significant level of intervention and an unprecedented level of support.

“Any criminal investigation is a matter for Police Scotland.”

Police Scotland has been approached for comment.

title: Trump, Putin, Xi issue 4-point declaration after historic summit
excerpt: Trilateral summit talks conclude in Shenzhen, China, as President Donald Trump wraps up an historic meeting with President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin. Heritage Foundation senior fellow St...
body_text:
Trilateral summit talks conclude in Shenzhen, China, as President Donald Trump wraps up an historic meeting with President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin. Heritage Foundation senior fellow Steve Yates joins 'Fox & Friends First' to analyze the geopolitical stakes.

President Donald Trump issued a joint "peace declaration" with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday following the trio's trilateral meeting during the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China.

"The three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security," the White House said in a statement, titled "U.S.-Russia-China Heads of State Declaration toward Peace."

Russia's Foreign Ministry and China's Chamber of Commerce to the EU confirmed the pact in near-identical statements, which also highlighted the three countries' commitment to reducing nuclear proliferation, increasing global petroleum production and upholding international institutions.

TRUMP'S HISTORIC SUMMIT WITH XI, PUTIN MARKS DIPLOMATIC MILESTONE, BUT BREAKTHROUGHS REMAIN ELUSIVE

"The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows," each of the U.S., Chinese and Russian statements read.

U.S. President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and China's President Xi Jinping greet each other before the welcome banquet for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting at the Shenzhen International Communication Center on November 18, 2026 in Shenzhen, China. (Iori Sagisawa-China Pool/Getty Images)

China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs also released a more expansive statement on the meeting.

TRUMP'S CHINA TRIP: HISTORIC XI-PUTIN TALKS, 'SUPERINTELLIGENCE' BOAST AND OTHER TOP MOMENTS

"President Xi noted that it is a groundbreaking move for the top leaders of China, Russia and the United States to hold the first-ever meeting in history. History tells us that peace among major countries brings stability to the world, while their contention would only lead to chaos in the world. Peace has been an enduring pursuit of humanity," the statement read.

The statement referred to the theme of the historic meeting between the three leaders, the first time in history the three nations' heads of state met collectively, as "Safeguarding World Peace and Promoting Strategic Stability in Major-Country Relations."

CHINA'S XI SURPRISES TRUMP AT TARMAC, RECIPROCATING GESTURE SHOWN MONTHS AGO

"More than 80 years ago, China, Russia and the United States, the key anti-fascist forces in the world, fought shoulder to shoulder and achieved great victories, winning peace and tranquility for the world. History is the best textbook; we must remember history, and learn from it to shape the future," the Chinese statement continued.

TRUMP CANNOT DETER XI AND PUTIN’S NUCLEAR GOALS WITH A STRATEGY DESIGNED FOR JUST ONE

All three countries' statements affirmed a commitment to nuclear harm reduction, with each including language stating that "a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought."

China's President Xi Jinping (C), US President Donald Trump (R) and Russia's President Vladimir Putin (L) take part in a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, on November 19, 2026. (Mandel NGAN / AFP via Getty Images)

Additionally, China's readout of the meeting stated that President Trump noted how many eyes around the world would be on the summit.

KIM JONG UN'S NUCLEAR BUILDUP SPARKS 'SERIOUS CONCERN' AHEAD OF TRUMP-XI-PUTIN SUMMIT

"President Trump noted that the U.S.-China-Russia summit draws attention from across the world. It is very important and has made history. The three countries are all nuclear-weapon states, and have a special and important responsibility to safeguard world peace and stability," the Chinese statement read.

An earlier Chinese readout of the meeting revealed topics covered on the agenda, which included Russia's war in Ukraine, ongoing tension in the Middle East and the Korean Peninsula.

CHINA BLOCKS BLOOMBERG REPORTER FROM TRUMP-PUTIN-XI MEETING OVER QUESTION TO TRUMP

US President Donald Trump (R) is greeted by China's President Xi Jinping as he arrives at Shenzhen Baoan International Airport to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, on November 18, 2026. (Mandel NGAN / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)

China also stressed that the summit was "positive, constructive and very productive."

"President Xi emphasized that the seeds sown at the summit today among the three presidents will surely take root, sprout, bloom and bear fruit," the statement concluded.

title: Troy Aikman fuels Joe Buck feud with another dig, creating Super Bowl-sized headache for ESPN

Troy Aikman just poured some more gasoline on an already burning hot fire for ESPN.

Amid tensions with his on-air broadcast partner, Joe Buck, Aikman took a dig at him during an appearance on a Dallas radio station. In his weekly hit on KTCK 96.7 The Ticket, Aikman noted that George Dunham’s usual partner, Craig Miller, was out and Dunham was flying solo.

"You know, Joe and I have a lot in common. I think this is the show I’ve always dreamed of," Dunham said. "Saw him on the country awards last night. He’s everywhere."

"Yeah ... everywhere. Ubiquitous," Aikman said with a laugh.

Sports commentators Troy Aikman and Joe Buck look on before a game between the Buffalo Bills and the Denver Broncos at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, N.Y., on Nov. 13, 2023. (Getty Images)

ESPN signed Buck to a new contract extension in Septembernbut did not sign Aikman. In October, the tensions boiled over when the pair argued off-air prior to a "Monday Night Football" game between the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams, according to multiple reports.

title: Florida Christians rebel against Imam's prayer opening a city meeting with a message of their own
excerpt: A group of Floridians showed up to a city commission meeting in the town of Bartow to protest an Imam’s invocation, praying the Lord’s Prayer in response to the Imam’s invitation. (Credit: Citizens De...
body_text:
A group of Floridians showed up to a city commission meeting in the town of Bartow to protest an Imam’s invocation, praying the Lord’s Prayer in response to the Imam’s invitation. (Credit: Citizens Defending Freedom)

An imam who was scheduled to deliver the invocation at a city commission meeting Monday evening in a southwest Florida town was interrupted by Christian protesters — who had a prayer of their own to share.

Footage from inside the meeting obtained by Fox News Digital shows dozens of Christian activists crowded into the back of a Bartow, Florida city commission meeting room. As Imam Sajid Bhuiya of the town's Masjid Al-Nur Mosque stepped up to the lectern to give the invocation, they began reciting the Lord's Prayer in unison. Some chants of "USA!" broke out, as well.

According to Robert Goodman, the southeast regional director of the conservative activist group Citizens Defending Freedom, news of Bhuiya's scheduled appearance began making the rounds on social media last weekend. He was among those who shared the news on social media. Goodman said about 100 people from different groups ended up attending the meeting.

IOWA CITY COUNCIL MEETING ERUPTS AFTER FORMER MEMBER OPENS WITH SATANIC PRAYER AND 'HAIL SATAN'

Christian protesters pack a city commission meeting in Bartow, Florida, as a local imam attempts to deliver the invocation. (Citizens Defending Freedom)

"Citizens Defending Freedom believes Christian voices deserve to be heard on matters affecting our communities, families, and freedoms, which is why we joined many other concerned citizens and organizations Monday night," Goodman told Fox News Digital.

He said the Quran teaches forced submission and permits men to strike their wives, while viewing the opinions of women as lesser than the opinions of men.

"We have every right to challenge teachings we believe conflict with human dignity, equality, religious liberty and America's founding principles, because we must be intolerant of intolerance while respecting every person's right to believe differently," he said.

Video from the city's official livestream of the event quickly went viral online.

PASTOR UNLEASHES ON DEARBORN AS RELIGIOUS TENSIONS ERUPT AT CITY COUNCIL MEETING: 'ENOUGH IS ENOUGH'

Some protesters made off-color comments, including telling Bhuiya to go back to his own country, which Goodman clarified that neither he nor his organization support.

"The disrespectful remarks made by two or three individuals Monday night do not represent me or Citizens Defending Freedom, because as Christians, we are called to speak truth with conviction and respect, not insults," Goodman said.

Goodman said Bhuiya was invited to deliver the invocation by a city official. Members of the commission mostly sat quietly, observing the commotion while police handled the crowd.

Police eventually escorted the Christian protesters out of the building, though no arrests were made.

Imam Sajid Bhuiya of Masjid Al-Nur Mosque delivering the invocation at a Bartow, Florida city commission meeting after being interrupted by Christian protesters. (Robert Goodman)

Bhuiya then spoke, quoting passages from the Quran that he said are meant to unify people. "This is a reminder that our differences in background, culture and faiths should not prevent us from treating one another with dignity," he said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Masjid Al-Nur Mosque for comment on the disruption of Bhuiya's invocation.

SWING STATE MAYOR SUED AS CITY’S MUSLIM HOLIDAY DISPLAYS IGNITE RELIGIOUS-FAVORITISM FIGHT

The city of Bartow released a statement explaining the Imam's appearance at the meeting.

The statement said that residents, "joined by individuals from other cities, attempted to prevent the imam from speaking and the Mayor from proceeding to conduct the business at hand."

A holy Christian cross laying on an open Bible with an American flag in the background. (iStock)

"For years, it has been tradition to open Bartow City Commission meetings with a prayer offered by either a faith-based leader or one of the City's elected officials," it said. "While historically the opening invocation/prayer is one based on Christian traditions, the opportunity is open to all faiths. This is consistent with the United States Constitution."

In the statement, city officials called for residents, "including religious leaders of all faiths, to come together to ensure that Bartow continues to be a welcoming place for all who live, work and play in Polk County's capital city."

Peter D'Abrosca is a politics reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Iraq reaches compromise with Kataib Hezbollah over armed group stronghold
excerpt: Iraq’s prime minister says security forces will establish a joint operations centre in the town of Jurf al-Sakhar, in a compromise with the Iranian-backed Kataib Hezbollah armed group over control of ...
body_text:
Iraq’s prime minister says security forces will establish a joint operations centre in the town of Jurf al-Sakhar, in a compromise with the Iranian-backed Kataib Hezbollah armed group over control of a strategic area south of Baghdad.

The Jurf al-Sakhar area has long been a stronghold of Kataib Hezbollah, and the new agreement comes after the Iraqi government announced plans to send in security forces amid allegations that Kataib Hezbollah was smuggling oil.

The compromise reached late on Thursday will see a new combined force deployed to the area, consisting of a brigade from the Iraqi Army, a brigade from the Federal Police, a regiment from the Energy Police to provide protection for oil pipelines in the area, and two brigades from the Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF) Commission, a collection of armed groups that are officially part of Iraq’s security forces, including some Kataib Hezbollah fighters.

In a statement, Iraq’s armed forces commander-in-chief said the new joint operations centre will open at 6am local time (03:00 GMT) on Friday morning.

A senior Iraqi official previously told Al Jazeera that Kataib Hezbollah had until Friday to leave Jurf al-Sakhar. The group had threatened to confront government troops, and had rejected the government’s efforts to disarm non-state militias.

Earlier in the week, an Iraqi official also told Al Jazeera that the commander of the Quds Force of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Esmail Qaani, arrived in Iraq to push for a solution due to the simmering tensions with Iran.

title: ‘Long term coup’ ousted Christians, conservatives from major watchdog, insider claims
excerpt: Former Southern Poverty Law Center executive Heidi Beirich faces federal charges of wire fraud and money laundering conspiracy. The Department of Justice alleges Beirich hid over $4 million in payment...
body_text:
Former Southern Poverty Law Center executive Heidi Beirich faces federal charges of wire fraud and money laundering conspiracy. The Department of Justice alleges Beirich hid over $4 million in payments from SPLC donors to fund White supremacy.

A former Southern Poverty Law Center official who led its hate-group tracking work told FBI agents he tried to make the watchdog’s controversial "Hate Map" more ideologically balanced, while saying Christians and conservatives were the first staffers pushed out in what he called a "long-term coup" at the organization after he left in 2013.

The former director said he pushed for a more evenhanded SPLC, arguing that its "Hate Map" — which lists conservative groups alongside Ku Klux Klan chapters — should also include left-wing extremists, including violent animal-rights and extremist environmental groups. However, the former director said the effort met resistance and that, as liberal leaders reshaped the organization, most of his 17-person team was replaced.

"There was some kind of coup, long-term coup going on there between some, what I would — what I heard were some pretty liberal people, extreme people that had other ideas about what we were doing," the unnamed former director told agents, as first reported by The Daily Signal's Tyler O'Neil, who has been covering the SPLC's legal troubles.

DOJ EXPANDS INDICTMENT AGAINST SPLC, ALLEGING $4M SECRETLY FUNNELED TO KKK AND EXTREMIST GROUPS

SPLC Intelligence Project Director Heidi Beirich speaks during an event on Jan. 12, 2018. (David Buchan/Variety/Penske Media via Getty Images)

The former director’s comments appeared in an FBI interview transcript filed as an exhibit to Dr. Heidi Beirich’s Nov. 2 court filing. Beirich, a former SPLC official charged alongside the organization in a federal case alleging a scheme to mislead donors and banks about donations used to pay informants associated with violent extremist groups, pointed to multiple FBI interviews with an unnamed former SPLC director, identified in the filing as "Individual-1."

In a January interview, Individual-1 told investigators he ran the SPLC’s field-source program, set up accounts used to pay sources and directed payments, according to Beirich’s filing. During a March 23 follow-up interview with Individual-1, FBI Special Agents David McDaniel and Parker Still framed the conversation around the program having "gone off the rails" under Beirich and told the former director they were not there to discuss the bank activity, noting he had "obviously nothing to do with all that," before questioning him about the SPLC’s alleged targeting of conservative organizations and Beirich’s role, according to the transcript.

EXCLUSIVE: SPLC'S 'FAR-LEFT,' 'ANTI-RACISM' CURRICULUM FOUND IN CLASSROOMS AS EARLY AS KINDERGARTEN: 'WATCHDOG'

Individual-1 responded that, as his "gut impression," he believed her actions were political and accused some liberals at the center of having "a good degree of hatred" for conservatism, according to the March 23 transcript.

Individual-1 also alleged a shift in power at the SPLC. After he left in 2013, he said, people were appointed to the SPLC’s board as "figureheads" and eventually gained enough voting power to take over the center. He said only one or two data-entry members of his roughly 17-person team remained, with the others replaced by staff he believed shared the new leadership’s politics.

"That's who they ran off first were the Christians and conservatives," the unnamed former director told agents when asked why Beirich took the actions she did after his departure. "Then they — then the rest they just replaced with people they liked, you know, that agreed with them politically."

HOW MUTINY AT SOUTHERN POVERTY LAW CENTER TRIGGERED LEADERSHIP COLLAPSE

The Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC) building seen in March 2020 in Montgomery, Alabama. (Barry Lewis/InPictures via Getty Images)

In separate comments about the SPLC's controversial "Hate Map," Individual-1 said he persuaded SPLC staff, despite internal resistance, to list Black separatist groups, which he considered comparable to White racist groups, on the map. However, he said he unsuccessfully pushed the SPLC to include violent animal-rights and environmental extremist groups and described his team’s approach during his tenure as director as "very nonpartisan" and "middle of the road."

"We were very nonpartisan, or at least when I was running things, when I was director, we stayed right in the middle of the road," he said.

In a June follow-up, the unnamed former director also criticized the SPLC's "Hate Map" for listing local chapters separately, saying it made the map's totals of the extremist groups it chose to identify look larger.

WATCH: SPLC CHIEF DOUBLES DOWN ON PLACING CHARLIE KIRK'S TURNING POINT USA ON 'HATE MAP'

While the unnamed former director was not charged in the SPLC case, Beirich was. Her lawyers say the interviews with the unnamed director warrant discovery into whether she was singled out because of her perceived role in the SPLC’s political speech, arguing that investigators’ questions about the SPLC’s treatment of conservative groups — and her alleged role in that work — could show the prosecution was motivated by hostility to the center’s political speech.

"Individual-1’s statements confirm my longstanding criticism of the Southern Poverty Law Center, that it exaggerates ‘hate’ by inflating the chapters on its ‘hate map’ and that it systematically demonizes conservatives and Christians while turning a blind eye to extremism on the Left," O’Neil, the author of "Making Hate Pay: The Corruption of the Southern Poverty Law Center," told Fox News Digital. "Now, we have the former director of the Intelligence Project saying the SPLC appears to have pushed out Christians and conservatives, while rejecting his suggestion to include environmentalist agitators on the map."

Fox News Digital reached out to the SPLC and attorneys for Heidi Beirich for comment but did not receive a response in time for publication.

Alec Schemmel is a Politics Reporter for Fox News Digital who is originally from Charlotte, North Carolina but now resides in the Washington D.C.-Baltimore Metro Area.

title: China could exploit US technology to threaten American forces, congressional watchdog leaders warn
excerpt:
Congressional watchdog leaders Randall Schriver and Mike Kuiken warn China could exploit American chips and AI to strengthen its military.

China's military could exploit advanced American technology,...
body_text:
Congressional watchdog leaders Randall Schriver and Mike Kuiken warn China could exploit American chips and AI to strengthen its military.

China's military could exploit advanced American technology, including through espionage and unauthorized access to artificial intelligence infrastructure, to develop weapons that could ultimately threaten U.S. forces, two congressional China watchdog leaders warned in an interview with Fox News Digital.

The officials raised concerns that Beijing is seeking to acquire sophisticated U.S. semiconductors and access powerful AI data centers, potentially strengthening its military capabilities without the knowledge or involvement of the American companies behind the technology.

Those concerns are underscored by the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission's 2026 annual report, which says Beijing is seeking to circumvent American export controls to obtain advanced semiconductors for military modernization.

BEYOND KILLER ROBOTS: CHINA'S REAL AI THREAT TO AMERICA IS ALREADY HERE, EXPERTS WARN

Racks of GPUs with a closed-loop liquid cooling system are seen inside an operational Microsoft data center in Indonesia on Feb. 4, 2026. (Yasuyoshi Chiba/AFP via Getty Images)

Citing an April 2026 assessment by Georgetown University's Center for Security and Emerging Technology, the commission reported that China's People's Liberation Army was soliciting advanced Nvidia chips for AI-enabled military capabilities.

The report describes Beijing's push toward "intelligentized warfare," integrating AI into weapons systems, targeting, military command and logistics.

Mike Kuiken, the commission's vice chairman, warned that the threat extends beyond chip exports to access to computing infrastructure abroad. "Anytime the Chinese gain access to advanced chips, we are helping them," Kuiken told Fox News Digital.

Commission Chairman Randall Schriver acknowledged the risk, pointing to permitted sales of dual-use technology, inadequate cybersecurity protections and American investments.

"I think we need sort of a comprehensive look at how the Americans are either wittingly or unwittingly contributing to Chinese military modernization," Schriver said.

Kuiken warned that Chinese AI developers or military institutions could also gain access to powerful data centers. "If we're doing it knowingly, we need to bring it to an end," he said.

TWO TOP TRUMP CABINET OFFICIALS GO TO WAR OVER CHINA SPY SCANDAL AMID EXPLOSIVE ACCUSATIONS: REPORT

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has pushed the Trump administration to ease restrictions on advanced AI chip sales to China, making the company’s technology a focal point in the U.S.-China race for AI leadership. (Kiyoshi Ota/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

The warnings come amid heightened scrutiny of Nvidia's relationship with China. Reuters reported Nov. 18, 2026, that Nvidia had stopped shipping licensed Hopper-generation AI data center chips to Chinese customers, according to interim CEO Colette Kress.

The findings also come amid a separate controversy surrounding Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned in November following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whom U.S. authorities have suspected of having intelligence ties to Beijing.

Jensen Huang has denied knowing about her alleged intelligence connections, while Beijing has rejected the espionage accusations. Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation. U.S. authorities have not conclusively established that Alice Huang was spying for Beijing, and Fox News Digital could not independently verify the allegations.

The commissioners also warned that China's advances extend beyond acquiring American hardware.

"Denial and deception is part of the CCP's standing doctrine, and that extends to the PLA, so I'm sure there are things we have yet to discover," Schriver said.

FOREIGN SPY ‘HONEYTRAPS’ TARGETING AMERICA’S TECH ELITE SPARK ALARM AMID NVIDIA CEO SCANDAL

He pointed to China's growing use of AI-enabled military systems, including autonomous unmanned platforms.

Kuiken warned that Beijing is increasingly integrating advanced AI into existing military technology. "We are absolutely seeing the PLA take the technologies that they have on the shelf today and figuring out how they can deploy the most advanced artificial intelligence capabilities into that ecosystem so that they can gain advantage," he said.

Against those concerns, China's Foreign Ministry struck a more cooperative tone regarding AI security in a Nov. 19, 2026, statement following a meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump in Shenzhen.

China's first AI-powered soccer tournament (CCTV)

CHINA WATCHDOG WARNS TRUMP FACES ‘2-ON-1’ SHOWDOWN WITH XI, PUTIN AS TAIWAN RISKS MOUNT

"China and the United States should strengthen communication and coordination, prevent the security risks of AI, and ensure that AI is always under human control," the ministry said in its account of Xi's remarks.

The commission also identifies protecting American data as a leading national security priority, warning that AI could make it easier to identify cybersecurity vulnerabilities and compromise sensitive information, amid a series of high-profile technology outages affecting major U.S. companies and government systems.

Asked about the recent disruptions involving the NSA, Apple and Chase Bank, Kuiken warned that increasingly sophisticated AI models are making it easier to identify cybersecurity weaknesses.

"These frontier models are incredibly good at cyber, which means they're good at coding and coding means it's very easy to find vulnerabilities in things," Kuiken told Fox News Digital. "You're basically seeing these leading organizations around the world do everything they can to lock down their organizations to make sure they're not vulnerable."

Kuiken emphasized that the commission's leading recommendation this year focuses on protecting American data, describing it as both a national security priority and an economic resource. "One, we want to protect it to keep ourselves secure and two, we wanna deploy it in the models that we have with the democratic world, controls to get economic benefit from it," he said.

The commissioners did not establish any connection between the recent technology outages and Chinese cyber operations.

An Amazon Web Services data center on Aug. 26, 2026, in Stone Ridge, Virginia. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House and the Chinese Embassy in Washington for comment but did not receive responses in time for publication.

Efrat (Effie) Lachter is a reporter for Fox News Digital with more than 15 years of experience covering conflict, global affairs, human rights and political accountability. She has directed and produced more than 200 documentary segments across more than 40 countries, documenting conflicts, humanitarian crises, corruption, human trafficking, gender-based violence and the human stories behind major world events.

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. Lachter is the recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award and was a 2023–2024 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She also won two Rockower Awards for Excellence in Reporting. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: Hakeem Jeffries on brink of House history as he tells Democrats to ‘fight Maga, not each other’ – US politics live
excerpt:
Democrats resoundingly nominated Jeffries to serve as speaker of the House when the new Congress is sworn in next year

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

Hakeem Jeffries said it is the ...
body_text:
Democrats resoundingly nominated Jeffries to serve as speaker of the House when the new Congress is sworn in next year

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

Hakeem Jeffries said it is the job of Democratic lawmakers to “fight Maga extremism” as he stood on the brink of becoming the first ever Black house speaker.

Democrats on Wednesday resoundingly nominated Jeffries to serve as speaker of the House when the new Congress is sworn in next year.

A New York congressman who has served as the Democratic minority leader since 2023, Jeffries is set to become one of Donald Trump’s most prominent opponents for the final two years of his presidency, when Democrats will control both the Senate and House of Representatives and are expected to undertake aggressive efforts to check his powers.

After his nomination was secured during closed-door voting, 251-11, ahead of a full House vote, Jeffries promised to take on the Trump administration’s Maga approach to governing the US. “Our job is to fight Maga extremism, not each other,” he said, “and to get big things done for the American people.”

Democrats nominated Jeffries despite concerns from some progressives that he represents a politically risky status quo for a party that is looking to capitalize on a surprisingly good performance in the midterms, where voters swept them back into power in the House and Senate with significant majorities.

He would become the first Democratic House speaker since Nancy Pelosi, who will retire from Congress at the end of this year.

Meanwhile today, president Trump has left China after hailing his trilateral meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, saying the three leaders were “really making history”. Trump said the US, Russia and China, the world’s largest nuclear powers, were “uniquely positioned” to discuss reducing their nuclear stockpiles.

During a fiery House hearing, Markwayne Mullin, the homeland security secretary, defended his decision to take a government plane to attend a college football game, while thousands of flights had been cancelled and the airspace closed during the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) nationwide grounding over the weekend. “You want to bring up the fact that I took my family and my great nieces to an [Lousiana State University] game that was scheduled for weeks prior because I wanted to be a good uncle,” Mullin said, following questions from Congressman Bennie Thompson, the homeland security committee’s top Democrat.

Elon Musk called his midterm political spending “foolish.” After pouring nearly half a billion dollars into the election, in a Wednesday conversation with The New York Times’s DealBook Summit, Musk said: “If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money.”

As legislators press for more answers on last week’s outage that caused thousands of flights to be halted, Duffy has continued finger-pointing, telling digital media outlet 2WAY on Wednesday that L3Harris, the aerospace and defense company whose router malfunctioned during an update, did not identify the issue “quick enough.”

Speaking to the media following a Berlin meeting of the Coalition of the Willing (a group of about 35 countries formed to offer financial and diplomatic support for Ukraine), Jared Kushner – Donald Trump’s special envoy and son-in-law – said that the US president dialed into the meeting with European allies.

This comes after Trump’s meeting with Vladimir Putin in Shenzen, China earlier today. Kushner did not reveal any details about the president’s summit, but said that Trump came away from the trilateral China meeting thinking “peace is achievable”.

My colleagues are covering the latest here:

Democrats are celebrating after, with Mary Peltola’s victory in Alaska, they have officially secured 56 Senate seats after the midterm elections. But Jamie Davis, who lost an incredibly close election for a Senate seat in Louisiana and could have made it 57, told the Guardian it “stings to come close”.

In Louisiana, which has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 2008, Davis lost to the Republican congresswoman Julia Letlow 49.1% to 50.9%. He was about 25,000 votes short in a state that cast about 1.5m votes.

“Truthfully, I mean, it kind of stings to come close, but what hurts more than anything else is the fact that, still today, people don’t realize and know what we did,” Davis said. “There are still some people out there right now today who do not realize that I only came within a point – I think it’s one point, 1.1 or 1.2 points of winning this election.”

Across the south, Democrats are now wondering what might have been, as other Senate seats were also close. Barry Moore beat Everett Wess in Alabama by nine points, which is a landslide in many states and a catastrophe compared with Donald Trump’s 30-point margin in 2024. Angie Nixon, whose progressive politics and opposition to the Israeli government looked like a mismatch with Florida’s conservative electorate, came within three points of unseating the Republican incumbent, Ashley Moody, in a special election.

In the weeks since, Democrats have questioned which of those states might have been winnable had the national party cast its light in the south. And many have zeroed in on Louisiana.

Unlike Florida, Louisiana is not an expensive media market. And Louisiana does not have the depth of partisan political identification to be overcome in a place like Alabama.

Turnout nationwide ran about three points higher in November than four years ago. In Louisiana, it ran eight points higher, in line with states facing competitive US Senate elections like Michigan and Maine.

Senator Bill Cassidy and Trump have long been at odds. Cassidy voted for his impeachment and asked him not to run in 2024. Trump targeted the Louisiana Republican in the primary, endorsing Letlow.

The Callais decision from the US supreme court originated in Louisiana and prompted the state to postpone primary elections and set off redistricting battles this year. Combined with Cassidy’s third-place finish in the primary, the motivating effect of these events on Black voters should have also set off alarm bells among Democratic fundraisers and operatives, Davis said.

“When it became open, that’s the time when Republicans and Democrats and independents all should have been on notice that there’s an open seat in the Senate,” Davis said. “And not just automatically think that the seat is going to turn to be Republican.”

Donald Trump said that he will hold a press conference at the White House on Friday at 12pm ET following a “great and highly consequential trip” to the Philippines and China, which included a trilateral summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.

The president announced the briefing on Truth Social, and also said he would discuss the trade deals he signed on his trip.

Republican Senate majority leader John Thune said Thursday that he’ll wait to see “what was discussed, and maybe what was agreed to” following Trump’s meeting in China with president Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin.

But Thune told reporters that “as far as I’m concerned, I’m with Ukraine” amid its war with Russia. Thune added he thinks most senators would agree with him.

“I think that’s going to be where most of my colleagues find themselves,” he said.

Donald Trump told NBC News he ⁠had discussed ⁠artificial ​intelligence (AI) with Chinese president Xi Jinping during ⁠his visit to China and the leaders ⁠both agreed that having guardrails ​was ‌good.

“We spoke ‌about SI, and we ‌both agreed that we want, we’re you know very much into SI, but we do ‌think that having guardrails, you know, at ​least on a minimal basis is a positive thing,” Trump said, ⁠using his preferred term for ​artificial intelligence, ​Super Intelligence, ​or SI.

Asked what “minimal ​basis” ‌meant, Trump ​said, “Well, ​we didn’t get into definitions.”

The Trump administration’s plans to build a “smart border wall” through a 500-mile stretch of Texas that includes the Big Bend national park recently got the green light from the supreme court. But those efforts are likely to slam into a big, blue wall.

Last week’s decision – the result of a continuing challenge to the administration’s decision to waive dozens of federal laws to speed wall construction in the Big Bend region – dealt a major blow to environmentalists and park enthusiasts, as well as locals who value the region’s remoteness, landowners who could see their properties devalued and businesses that rely on outdoor tourism.

But the ruling also came less than a week after Republicans suffered staggering losses in the midterms – including the once-in-a-generation flipping of Texas from red to blue. The state elected a Democratic governor after more than 30 years, and its first Democratic senator since the 1980s. The blue tsunami that handed both chambers of the US Congress to the Democrats with sizable majorities also flipped the Texas state house and weakened Republican control over the state senate.

That could all throw a wrench in the Trump administration’s plans.

The border wall is a federal project, so the White House will still have a great deal of power to push it forward. But for the first time, US Customs and Border Protection (CBP), the agency overseeing construction, will now face open hostility from the Lone Star state’s government as it contemplates resuming building efforts.

“Texas sovereignty and land should be protected,” Gina Hinojosa, the governor-elect, said in response to the ruling. “By letting the federal government bulldoze our land, the supreme court is continuing to put corporate profits before the people of Texas.”

Former president Barack Obama told newly elected House Democrats to not “get complacent” at a private reception hosted by Hakeem Jeffries, the current minority leader and likely House speaker in the new Congress. According to several reports, Obama was the special guest at an event that incoming members were ferried to in buses away from Capitol Hill on Wednesday, where he told the soon-to-be lawmakers, several of whom flipped Republican-held seats and won gerrymandered seats, to “hang on to your values, your commitments, your convictions”.

“Push for what you believe in, but understand the job you’ve taken is in a democracy. You’ve got to figure out how to actually get shit done with your colleagues,” Obama added. “And they’re not all representing the same constituencies that you are, and you want them to keep winning because that’s how you stay in a majority, and actually, over the long term, get stuff done.”

As the US catches up on Donald Trump’ shistoric trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping of China and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, the likely House speaker Hakeem Jeffries has weighed in on the summit.

“The President treats Russia like a friend and Canada like a foe,” Jeffries wrote on social media. “America just elected a Congress that knows it’s the exact opposite.”

The National Security Agency is seeing a third day of disruptions to its internal network, NSA Net, which allows staff to share highly classified information with each other, according to the New York Times.

The Times reports that employees at the NSA’s Maryland headquarters are under “code orange” for Thursday day shift, which requires non-essential workers are to stay home unless contacted by their supervisors.

Earlier this week the NSA said that it experienced a “temporary degradation” during scheduled routine maintenance, after reports that NSA Net had gone down.

In a statement, the agency said some internal systems were affected but that “mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational” and its ability to defend national security continues.

However, the NSA did not say what caused the outage, and whether the system was back to normal.

Over the coming weeks, Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen, along with any late challengers, will vie for the party’s top Senate leadership post before lawmakers cast their votes. Here are four things to know about how the election works.

A secret, closed-door election: Unlike the public speaker of the House vote, where lawmakers cast ballots on the chamber floor, the Senate leadership contest takes place behind closed doors. Senators vote by secret ballot, and individual votes are not disclosed.

The winner only needs a caucus majority: The Democratic leadership race is decided solely by members of the party’s Senate caucus. Now that Democrats are set to have 56 seats in the new year, the winner will need secure 29 votes for the top role.

The vote is scheduled for next month: As things stand, the election is set for 1 December. Both incumbent senators and incoming Democratic members will participate, while retiring and outgoing senators will not vote, despite many having publicly weighed in on the race.

Republicans choose their leaders separately: Republicans hold their own closed-door leadership elections in both chambers. Earlier this month, House Republicans selected hardliner Jim Jordan as their leader after Mike Johnson opted not to run for minority leader. In the Senate, Republicans unanimously backed John Thune to continue leading the conference.

Following the news that Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be the next House speaker, leading to a full chamber vote which he is likely to win in the new year, it’s worth turning our attention to the ongoing battle in the upper chamber.

Here, top Democrats Chuck Schumer is vying to become Senate majority leader but is facing a challenge from progressive Chris Van Hollen. Despite the fact that Schumer is confident he has the votes to succeed, a number of lawmakers have pledged support for Van Hollen and say there needs to be change from leadership when Democrats take control of the Senate in the new year.

On Wednesday, Van Hollen said in a video on social media that he is continuing to meet with members one-on-one, and any discussion about expediting the closed-door vote to select the leader on 1 December has been quashed.

“We need to use this opportunity to change the way the Senate Democratic caucus does business,” Van Hollen said.

Attorney general Todd Blanche’s wife, Kristine Blanche, who was appointed earlier this year to a US government advisory board on alternative medicine, has a website on which she marketed dietary supplements and treatments with unproven medical and health claims.

Blanche is a licensed physician assistant who says she has a PhD in breast thermography from the University of Science, Arts and Technology in Montserrat, a British territory in the Caribbean. She is also an advocate for alternative medical cures and holistic health.

Her site also links to a page called “Dr Blanche’s Dispensary”, where patients can buy supplement pills she recommends. She suggested that one product, a liquid herbal compound, could be used to treat the Epstein-Barr virus, although she misspelled “Epstein”.

There is no medication approved by the FDA to treat or cure Epstein-Barr, and the product itself does not claim to treat the virus.

Blanche also listed five supplements in her store, priced up to $63 a bottle, which she said can help treat human papillomavirus (HPV).

Another treatment Blanche offers, priced online at $595, claims to help men “boost” their testosterone levels and lose weight.

An anti-vaccine group led for years by Robert F Kennedy Jr said Meta has “taken down” posts on its accounts, after a Guardian report found the group was sharing false and misleading information about vaccines.

The Guardian reported on Wednesday that Children’s Health Defense (CHD) had earlier this year been allowed back on Facebook and Instagram, four years after Meta removed it from Facebook and Instagram for repeatedly violating its misinformation policies.

CHD said in posts on X that within hours of the Guardian’s article running, “ALL of our accounts have been targeted”. It accused Meta of censorship.

“Our posts are being taken down AGAIN simply for sharing the truth about vaccines and the experiences of families whose children were injured by vaccines,” CHD posted on Wednesday night, adding: “People have every right to discuss vaccine injuries and share their experiences without being silenced by big tech.”

Meta and CHD did not immediately return emails seeking comment.

Among the content that was no longer up as of Wednesday evening was a video that the group had posted on Facebook that said the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine is “not so safe and effective”.

Another video no longer available had been titled “Vaccines: Your child could die”, and made the misleading claim that vaccines are deadly.

A third video that was no longer up said the HPV vaccines are “very dangerous”, have “caused hundreds, thousands of deaths”, and do not prevent cervical cancer.

All three posts had been visible on CHD accounts at the time the Guardian story was published on Wednesday.

Chinese state media has issued a four-point “peace declaration by the Chinese, Russian and US leaders” following their meeting.

The same statement was later issued by Russia.

Chinese president Xi Jinping, Russian president Putin and US president Trump held a meeting in Shenzhen on 19 November 2026. The Russian and US leaders expressed their gratitude to China for hosting this historic meeting. The three heads of state exchanged in-depth views on the current international situation and committed themselves to maintaining strategic stability and international security.

1. As permanent members of the UN security council, China, Russia and the US are committed to promoting UN reform so that it may respond more effectively to global challenges and fulfil its fundamental mission of maintaining international peace and security.

2. The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows.

3. The three heads of state recognised that the principle of state consent and respect for the immunity of state officials are of paramount importance, and agreed that the international criminal court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction.

4. The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must not be fought. The three countries will engage in dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing nuclear proliferation.

Elon Musk denied being Maga on Wednesday, despite aligning himself intensely with Donald Trump’s Make America Great Again movement since 2024.

“I’m not Maga,” the world’s richest person told the New York Times Dealbook summit, which he attended via video call from China, where he is one of several US business leaders who have accompanied Trump on his trip to Asia.

“I’m not sure what Maga means, but if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican party, then I certainly don’t have that,” the chief executive of SpaceX and Tesla added.

Musk famously declared at a 2024 campaign rally in Madison Square Garden: “I’m not just Maga. I’m dark, gothic Maga.”

In a 45-minute interview with Andrew Ross Sorkin, a New York Times columnist, Musk also said it would be good for Washington to have split control between the two parties, and that he thinks “there are positives and negatives in both”.

He also accused Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, of “lying” about restrictions on access to his firm’s Starshield satellite system; praised Jensen Huang, the ousted Nvidia chief executive; and said that “no one I met at Anthropic set off my evil detector”.

Asked about his previous negative comments about Anthropic, Musk said that before he agreed to rent computing power to the AI firm: “I went to met with a lot of people at Anthropic. I didn’t just move forward with the deal.”

“My interaction so far with the Anthropic team is that they seem like good people and they seem principled,” Musk added. “They seem diligent and they seem seem to care about the future.”

Musk donated at least $250m of his own money to help Trump win the election in 2024, and recently spent nearly $500m in the US midterms to support Republicans, many of whom lost.

Denmark’s parliament on Thursday approved a hard-wrought agreement with Greenland and the United States to strengthen security in the Arctic and North Atlantic.

The vote follows months of pressure by president Donald Trump seeking to control Greenland, a semiautonomous territory of Denmark, a Nato ally.

The trilateral deal - between Trump and the Danish and Greenlandic leaders – paves the way for more US bases in Greenland and eases tensions over Trump’s repeated calls for the vast island to become part of the US.

The 109-0 vote in the Folketing amounts to a final step, with the deal expected to enter into force once Denmark and Greenland has signed on. Greenland’s parliament approved the deal earlier this month, also with no opposition.
